en: Itivuttaka 35 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then the venerable Ānanda, having understood: "The Teacher has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling," approached the Blessed One at the proper time, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this, what was the meaning of that statement? "Ānanda, when I rose from my seat and entered my dwelling after saying this, I had these two thoughts in mind: 'If I were to teach the Dhamma to others, they would not understand me; that would be wearying for me, that would be troublesome. And also: 'The Tathāgata is alone, he delights in being alone; the Tathāgata is secluded, he delights in seclusion. "But, venerable sir, why does the Blessed One say: 'If I were to teach the Dhamma to others, they would not understand me; that would be wearying for me, that would be troublesome'? "Ānanda, this Dhamma is profound, difficult to see, difficult to comprehend, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of mere reasoning, subtle, and intelligible only to the wise. But this generation delights in attachment, takes pleasure in attachment, is devoted to attachment. For such a generation, this state—devoid of attachment, detached from the world, relinquishing all bases, the cessation of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna—is difficult to see.

And this generation delights in clinging, takes pleasure in clinging, is devoted to clinging. For such a generation, this state—devoid of clinging, detached from the world, relinquishing all bases, the cessation of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna—is difficult to see. And this generation delights in becoming, takes pleasure in becoming, is devoted to becoming. For such a generation, this state—devoid of becoming, detached from the world, relinquishing all bases, the cessation of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna—is difficult to see. Therefore, Ānanda, when I thought: 'If I were to teach the Dhamma to others, they would not understand me; that would be wearying for me, that would be troublesome,' it was with reference to this that I said so. "But, venerable sir, there are beings with little dust in their eyes who are perishing through not hearing the Dhamma. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma. "Therefore, Ānanda, I shall now set forth the foundation of the teaching, and you may expound the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by existence, birth comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by clinging, existence comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by craving, clinging comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by feeling, craving comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by contact, feeling comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by the sixfold base, contact comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by mentality-materiality, the sixfold base comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by consciousness, mentality-materiality comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by name-and-form, consciousness comes to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'Conditioned by ignorance, volitional formations come to be. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no birth, aging-and-death does not come to be; with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no existence, birth does not come to be; with the cessation of existence, birth ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no clinging, existence does not come to be; with the cessation of clinging, existence ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no craving, clinging does not come to be; with the cessation of craving, clinging ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no feeling, craving does not come to be; with the cessation of feeling, craving ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no contact, feeling does not come to be; with the cessation of contact, feeling ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no sixfold base, contact does not come to be; with the cessation of the sixfold base, contact ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no mentality-materiality, the sixfold base does not come to be; with the cessation of mentality-materiality, the sixfold base ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no consciousness, mentality-materiality does not come to be; with the cessation of consciousness, mentality-materiality ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there is no name-and-form, consciousness does not come to be; with the cessation of name-and-form, consciousness ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. What, Ānanda, is that foundation of the teaching? It is: 'When there are no volitional formations, ignorance does not come to be; with the cessation of volitional formations, ignorance ceases. Thus, Ānanda, you should teach the Dhamma as you have heard it and mastered it. Then the venerable Ānanda, having delighted and rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him on his right, departed. Then the venerable Ānanda, having spent the rest of the night in the open air, approached the Blessed One at the proper time, paid homage to him
The Discourse on Deceit Regarding the First Birth.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

"Monks, this holy life is not lived for the sake of deceiving people, nor for the sake of flattering people, nor for the sake of gain, honor, and renown, nor with the thought: 'Let people know me thus.'"
"Moreover, monks, this holy life is lived for the sake of restraint and for the sake of abandoning.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. With reference to this, it is said:
“For the sake of restraint and for the sake of abandonment,
the Blessed One taught the holy life that is not based on mere tradition.”
This path, leading down into the depths of Nibbāna,
has been followed by the great ones, the great seers.
Whoever practices it as taught by the Buddha will make an end of suffering.
“Those who act according to the Teacher’s instruction.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
